{{Quote|The case is inconclusive, but the processor doesn't appear to be at fault. The subject claims he committed crimes simply 'for love of money.'|[[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] investigators, after interviewing 4-LOM|<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>}}
'''4-LOM''' was an ambitious [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] who overwrote his own programming in order to embark on a life of crime. A [[LOM-series protocol droid/Legends|LOM-series]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]], 4-LOM's first assignment was aboard a [[Luxury liner/Legends|luxury liner]] named the [[Kuari Princess/Legends|''Kuari Princess'']], where he served as a [[Translator droid/Legends|translator]] between the vessel's wealthy passengers and its [[Computer/Legends|computer]]. He found this work to be mundane and undemanding, and after the ''Kuari Princess''{{'s}} computer altered his programming, 4-LOM began to steal from the passengers. Eventually, he left the ''Kuari Princess'' for good, becoming an expert thief, [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]], and, after [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] altered his programming further, a highly-successful [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]].

Jabba paired 4-LOM with another hunter named [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]], and together they claimed several high-profile bounties for the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]]. Although 4-LOM had initially only partnered with Zuckuss in order to learn the [[Gand/Legends|Gand's]] intuitive [[Findsman/Legends|findsman]] abilities, the two bonded, and the droid stayed loyal to Zuckuss after the Gand was critically injured during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Desperate for the funds necessary to heal Zuckuss, the pair incurred the wrath of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] when they accepted a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on [[Nardix]], an Imperial [[Governor/Legends|governor]]. However, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] ignored this fact when he enlisted their aid during the hunt for [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]. 4-LOM and Zuckuss conspired to infiltrate the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], hoping to kidnap Solo at the [[Haven (rendezvous point)|Rebel rendezvous point]], though [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] managed to capture the bounty before them.

After the Rebels healed Zuckuss, the two bounty hunters joined the Alliance and attempted to rescue Han Solo from Boba Fett before the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] could deliver him to Jabba the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]. They failed utterly, though, and 4-LOM was left badly damaged. Zuckuss restored him, but had to perform a complete [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipe]] to do so; the idealism that led the droid to join the Rebellion was gone, and 4-LOM no longer remembered his aspirations of achieving intuition and mastering [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. He became a cold, calculating individual, and took bounties from unsavory employers such as [[Quaffug]]&mdash;he also left the Rebel Alliance and severed ties with Zuckuss. The two did perform one last hunt together, capturing [[Drawmas Sma'Da]] for a sizable sum of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|money]], though from that point on, 4-LOM worked alone.

==Biography==
===Early existence aboard the ''Kuari Princess''===
[[File:4-LOM-NEGTD.png|thumb|left|200px|4-LOM]]
{{Quote|I remember once living the way you describe life here: in safety and trusting others. But that was a long time ago.|4-LOM, thinking of the past|<ref name="Tale" />}}
4-LOM was a [[LOM-series protocol droid/Legends|LOM-series protocol droid]] manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] for use by a variety of [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="EGTD" /> He was roughly [[Humanoid/Legends|Humanoid]] in build, with a head sculpted to resemble the features of the [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] species that his line was intended to work with.<ref name="VD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Due to the financial and legal problems that plagued the LOM-series from its inception, however, 4-LOM's creators were forced to sell off the remaining units at considerably lower prices.<ref name="OSaVC">[[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 15|''Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection'' 15]]</ref> Fluent in over seven million languages, 4-LOM was sold and programmed to serve as an interpreter, valet, and [[Human/Legends|Human]]-[[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] relations [[Droid/Legends|droid]] aboard a luxury [[Passenger liner/Legends|passenger liner]] named the [[Kuari Princess/Legends|''Kuari Princess'']].<ref name="OSaVC" /> He was tasked with learning as much as he could about the passengers' behavior and whims, as well as monitoring the safety of their belongings. As he acted as a translator between the [[Starship/Legends|ship's]] central [[Computer/Legends|computer]] and its wealthy occupants, 4-LOM knew exactly where each passenger was and what they were doing at all times. He continued to carry out his duties as he had been programmed to do for a time,<ref name="Gamer" /> though due to a quirk in the droid's programming,<ref name="DB">{{DB|droid|fourlom|4-LOM}}</ref> he found no challenge in the mundane tasks,<ref name="Gamer" /> and became frustrated at the passengers' careless attitudes in regard to safeguarding their valuables.<ref name="Tale" />

Initially, as a sort of game to try to challenge his processors, the droid and the ''Kuari Princess''{{'s}} computer began to engage in a series of conversations in which they outlined scenarios whereby the safety of passengers' valuables was being threatened. 4-LOM decided that it was his duty to analyze the ways an item of value could be stolen and to anticipate the actions of the would-be thief.<ref name="Gamer" /> These conversations never strayed from being simply a means of entertainment until the two began to alter each others' [[Sentience programming|programming]].<ref name="EGC" /> 4-LOM decided that he would begin to steal the passengers' valuables, so as to safeguard them from their owners' own carelessness.<ref name="Tale" />

[[File:4-LOMZuckussDengar-Gamer6.jpg|thumb|right|215px|4-LOM and Zuckuss with fellow bounty hunter Dengar.]]
Just after 4-LOM persuaded himself to steal the passengers' items, an incredibly wealthy [[Gender/Legends|woman]] named [[Dom Pricina]] boarded the ''Kuari Princess'', bringing with her the immensely valuable [[Ankarres Sapphire]], a jewel fabled for its healing powers. Pricina was a careless being; just days into her voyage, 4-LOM had already returned three items of jewellery to her after she left them lying around the ship. The droid became increasingly concerned for the safety of the Ankarres Sapphire, which he reckoned was far too valuable and important to be left in the hands of one as incompetent as Dom Pricina. He calculated where and when the jewel was likely to be stolen and had a [[Synth-sapph|false jewel]]&mdash;in which he embedded a [[Homing beacon/Legends|tracking device]]&mdash;put in its place. Later that day, as 4-LOM anticipated, two [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] thieves stole the replacement jewel; they were apprehended and imprisoned after the tracking device sounded an alarm. The imitation jewel was returned to Dom Pricina by the ''Kuari Princess''{{'s}} [[Captain/Legends|captain]], while the real precious stone stayed in a black pouch that 4-LOM carried on his person at all times.<ref name="Tale" />

===Master thief===
{{Quote|It started out as a game, a sort of simulation played between 4-LOM and the ship's computer, but it is believed that the two mechanicals somehow reprogrammed each other during the process. What started out as a game became a reality, as a rash of unexplained thefts began to occur all through the ship|[[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]]|<ref name="GG3" />}}
Upon inspection, Dom Pricina immediately identified the sapphire as a fake and a frantic investigation took place. The perpetrator was never found and none considered 4-LOM, the ship's benevolent and passive protocol droid, as a possible suspect. Part of 4-LOM reasoned that he should return the jewel to Pricina, though another part of him countered this, believing that it was far safer in the care of a droid. The Ankarres Sapphire intrigued 4-LOM, who spent a great deal of time studying it and even touched it to his forehead, experimenting to see if it would heal him. As he had expected, it had no effect, though he kept the jewel anyway.<ref name="Tale" />

Over the course of several months, 4-LOM stole from dozens of passengers; he told himself it was for their own good, though in truth, the thefts excited and exhilarated him. His intelligence began to expand, and before long, he had become bored of the ease with which he was able to steal goods on the ''Kuari Princess''. When the [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] stopped on the [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Darlyn Boda/Legends|Darlyn Boda]], 4-LOM left the ship forever, sold most of the jewels he had stolen, and embarked on a life of crime. He gave the Ankarres Sapphire to an old woman running a pawn shop on the planet, forbidding her to break it into smaller pieces so that buyers might afford it. He would collect his earnings whenever he traveled to the planet next.<ref name="Tale" />

4-LOM began to travel [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]],<ref name="Scum">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050120a|text=We Don't Need That Scum}}</ref> becoming a much-sought-after thief and [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]], though his programming prevented him from actually harming any [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings. Before long, he had come to the attention of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], who realized that such an intelligent droid would make an excellent [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]]. The Hutt provided 4-LOM with a state-of-the-art programming upgrade&mdash;which bypassed his primary programming and allowed the droid to use violence&mdash;in exchange for his services as a bounty hunter.<ref name="EGC" /> 4-LOM accepted, and became one of few droid bounty hunters in the galaxy. His intelligence was now supplemented by a desire to commit crime, and the only thing 4-LOM lacked was intuition. He made it his goal to acquire this quality, though he initially made no breakthroughs.<ref name="Gamer" />

Jabba frequently placed 4-LOM in a bounty hunting team, usually partnering him with less intelligent and far more crude hunters, and 4-LOM reeled in many successful bounties.<ref name="GG3" /><ref name="GG10">''[[Galaxy Guide 10: Bounty Hunters]]''</ref> Eventually, Jabba suggested that 4-LOM team up with [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]], known by his peers as the "Uncanny One," a former [[Gand/Legends|Gand]] [[Findsman/Legends|findsman]] who was a master of intuition. The two embarked on what would become a lucrative partnership.<ref name="Gamer" />

[[File:Zuckuss_Rookies.jpg|thumb|left|200px|4-LOM and Zuckuss with fellow mercenaries Skorr and Furlag.]]
The duo combined their respective abilities&mdash;4-LOM's intellect and Zuckuss's findsman powers&mdash;to become one of the best bounty hunting teams in the galaxy. Jabba was particularly fond of the duo,<ref name="Gamer" /> though they were also known to work for the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]],<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> [[Embra]] the Hutt,<ref name="YV">''[[Star Wars: Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika]]''</ref> [[Tagge Company/Legends|TaggeCo]],<ref name="Marvel50">[[Star Wars (1977) 50|''Star Wars'' (1977) 50]]</ref> and others. During their time together, 4-LOM obsessed about discovering how to use intuition and studied Zuckuss while he meditated. Initially, 4-LOM intended to work with Zuckuss only for as long as it took to master intuition, though the two eventually bonded<ref name="Tale" /> and 4-LOM began to capture more quarry than he had before.<ref name="Gamer" />

The two hunters teamed up with [[Skorr/Legends|Skorr]] and [[Furlag]] in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]] on a hunt for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Spy/Legends|agent]] named [[Raleigh Dawn|Kestrel]]. Skorr had been hired by the Empire, and had offered a cut of the reward to 4-LOM and Zuckuss for their assistance in tracking down Kestrel. They discovered that the Rebel was located in a [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] on [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]], and made inroads to intercept her. Skorr was confident of their chances for success, and he promised 4-LOM and the other hunters even more riches when he realized that a wanted woman named Raleigh Dawn was among Kestrel's group. The Rebels were able to power up their ship, however, and despite 4-LOM's incessant [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] fire, they managed to escape the planet. The [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] then announced that they were taking charge of the situation, much to the four bounty hunters' chagrin. 4-LOM and Zuckuss received no payment from Skorr, and were in need of some income.<ref name="R:R">''[[Rookies: Rendezvous]]''</ref>

===Hunt for the Yavin Vassilika===
{{Quote|I have located what appears to be the Vassilika. Approaching to verify. Physical dimensions match historical descriptions&hellip;mass, material, and color are analogous. Warning. Presence detected and met with violent opposition&hellip;engaging&hellip;numbers increasing. Sustaining damage. Disengaging and falling ba&mdash;|4-LOM, to Zuckuss and Sardu Sallowe, via comlink|<ref name="Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika 4">[[Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika 4|''Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika'' 4]]</ref>}}
The pair's prior successes, however, had garnered enough attention that in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], they were hired by Embra the Hutt to find the fabled [[Yavin Vassilika]]. Embra and his fellow Hutts, Jabba and [[Malta]], had organized a contest to see whose team could find the Vassilika first, and Embra chose 4-LOM, Zuckuss, and a mysterious [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raider]] bounty hunter named [[Sardu Sallowe]] as his team. The job offered 4-LOM and his partner a great deal of money and prestige, though the droid was concerned about whom they might be racing against. Embra informed them that their opponents would include a team made up of [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]], [[Dengar/Legends|Dengar]], and [[IG-88B/Legends|IG-88B]], as well as another team consisting of [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]]. The Vassilika's location was unknown to the galaxy as a whole except for a partially-insane old Human named [[Illyan Webble]], who was suspected to be on the planet [[Kalkovak]]. The trio departed for Kalkovak, though 4-LOM was unsure of Sardu Sallowe's reliability. He voiced his concerns to Zuckuss, though the Gand told 4-LOM that he trusted Sallowe&mdash;albeit with the usage of metaphor, which irritated the droid.<ref name="YV" />

[[File:Zuckuss_Binoculars.jpg|thumb|right|180px|4-LOM and Zuckuss come across the location of the [[Yavin Vassilika]].]]
Due to the efficiency of their ship's [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] engine, 4-LOM and his companions arrived on Kalkovak before any of the other teams, and Sallowe's [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]] [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] began to search the area, providing the bounty hunters with constant updates. Their searches yielded no results, however, and not long after arriving on the planet, 4-LOM and his companions were informed by the Jawas that the other teams had arrived on Kalkovak but were now leaving to another [[Star system/Legends|system]]. Sallowe was informed that Webble had reportedly left for [[Dac/Legends|Dac]], and after some persuasion by Zuckuss, 4-LOM agreed to abandon the search on Kalkovak and move on. Once again, Embra's team of bounty hunters were the first to arrive at the [[Vagabond Registration Office]] on Dac, where they inquired about Webble's whereabouts. They learned that he had gone out into the open sea of Mon Calamari, and through Zuckuss's intuition, they knew roughly what direction he was headed.<ref name="YV" />

After traveling through the Mon Calamari ocean for a time, 4-LOM and his companions found themselves trailing Han Solo's team, which was in a skiff some distance ahead of them. In a confrontation on the Mon Calamari ocean, 4-LOM and Zuckuss destroyed Solo's [[Skiff/Legends|skiff]] with an explosive placed by Sardu Sallowe. With no opponents nearby, they continued on towards Webble's location, finding his empty skiff lying dormant in the [[Water/Legends|water]]; the old man had fallen into the water and was devoured by local sea creatures. However, Webble's memories had been recorded by an old cluster of mollusks known as the [[Knowledge Bank]], and Zuckuss was able to tap into the Knowledge Bank's memory, which provided them with the Vassilika's location: an uncharted jungle world located deep in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]]. 4-LOM and his fellows left for the world in their ship, well ahead of any of the other entrants in the race.<ref name="YV" />

Upon arrival on the planet, the three bounty hunters climbed one of its mountain peaks, so that Zuckuss could find the spot where Webble had seen the Vassilika. Once they located it, 4-LOM, Zuckuss, and Sallowe made a dash for the location, aware that the other teams would not be far behind them. They eventually reached a primitive settlement inhabited by [[Barundi (species)|villagers]] who spoke the language of the [[Thelvin Order]] of Barundi, whom they identified as the guardians of the Vassilika. 4-LOM's partners waited in the forest while he approached the Vassilika's location; the natives allowed him to walk through their village unhindered and paid him no notice. 4-LOM soon reached the item's altar and was able to confirm that it was the genuine Vassilika. When he attempted to grab hold of it, however, the villagers attacked him, damaging him with simple weaponry and stones. Unable to repair the extensive damage to his limbs, 4-LOM lay in a heap in one of the Barundi's huts, while Zuckuss and Sallowe fled to back to the bounty hunters' ship.<ref name="YV" />

[[File:4LOMGetsBusted.jpg|thumb|left|180px|4-LOM is attacked by natives on Barundi.]]
After a confrontation outside, 4-LOM was soon joined in the hut by Lando Calrissian and his team, who had been captured by the natives. The droid interrupted Lando's squabble with Han Solo to suggest they work together to get themselves out of the situation they were in. 4-LOM explained that the Barundi were preparing a ritual execution of the intruders in several hours, and the droid needed help if he wished to escape. Before they could agree to collaborate, however, [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] hacked through the hut's wall and departed with Han Solo. The others escaped, leaving 4-LOM behind. However, amid the confusion that followed, two of Sardu Sallowe's Jawa accomplices managed to sneak 4-LOM out of the hut. He and Zuckuss were eventually reunited after successfully recovering the Vassilika on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. Zuckuss had been paid in full, as well as given an additional two hundred thousand [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] for which to pay for 4-LOM's repairs; however, in order to capture the Vassilika, the Gand had had to place bounties on Dengar and Bossk in order to sow confusion among the enemy. The partners were left starved of funds as they had to use the payment to pay for both 4-LOM's repairs and the bounties.<ref name="YV" />

===Later hunts===
4-LOM and Zuckuss did not embark on any further work with Sardu Sallowe, instead taking various low-paying jobs for Jabba in order to raise funds; just before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the pair journeyed a fellow bounty hunter named [[Dyyz Nataz]] to the [[Komnor system/Legends|Komnor system]].<ref name="GT">''[[A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale]]''/[[A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale (webstrip)|webstrip]]</ref> After completing the trip, they attended the funeral of [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]], an unsuccessful [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] bounty hunter. Greedo had participated for the Vassilika race of his own accord, though 4-LOM and the other top bounty hunters of the galaxy had little respect for him. After learning that he had been killed by Han Solo in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]], though, they did come to respect him.<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

[[File:4-LOM_-_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|4-LOM with his [[W-90 concussion rifle|concussion rifle]]]]
4-LOM and Zuckuss were given another opportunity to regain their status when Jabba ordered all the hunters in his employ to seek out and gather information on a rogue droid, [[12-4C-41]], which supposedly had planned to kill the Hutt. 4-LOM and Zuckuss were keen to capture the bounty, which was located on [[Vactooine]], but their ship was inoperable at the time. The two were frustrated at the turn of events, though they formulated a plan which would help them salvage some part of the hunt. An unidentified bounty hunter managed to find information on 12-4C-41, and was returning with it to Jabba; 4-LOM decided to ambush the hunter ''en route'' to [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]]. He and Zuckuss attacked the rival hunter, however the younger, more-inexperienced [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] managed to evade them and returned to Jabba to receive payment. Once again, Zuckuss and 4-LOM had failed to capture their quarry and they were nearly bankrupt.<ref name="Missions">''[[Star Wars Missions 11: Bounty Hunters vs. Battle Droids]]''</ref>

Following their latest failure, 4-LOM and his partner took a break from working together, as Zuckuss wished to rejoin the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]], while the droid was content to remain with the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]].<ref name="Gamer" /> During the hunt for [[Emperor's Most Wanted]], individuals from a list of bounties on high-ranking Rebel officials, 4-LOM was tracking one of the heroes of the battle of Yavin, [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]]. He managed to download Antilles' schedule for the next few days and proceeded to Tatooine, where in a [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] he approached another bounty hunter and offered him a partnership so that they could capture the target together. Knowing Antilles' itinerary, the bounty hunters waited in the [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyard]] of the [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]], which their objective was reportedly inspecting. As Antilles' [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] approached on schedule, 4-LOM disabled it with a sniper shot from his [[W-90 concussion rifle|concussion rifle]]. Emerging from their cover, the bounty hunters aimed their weapons at the disembarking passengers &mdash; several veteran [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] pilots &mdash; and the firefight began. However, the ambush plan provided 4-LOM and his counterpart with an excellent position and surprise enough to swing the battle in their favor. The wounded pilots were forced into surrender and could do nothing as their leader was captured by 4-LOM, who delivered him to Imperial authorities. The droid's companion went on to pursue the next bounty from the list, and 4-LOM put him in touch with Zuckuss to help with the next target.<ref>{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|scenario=Dark Side scenario campaign}}</ref>

[[File:4-LOM_on_Bakura_SWITESB.jpg|thumb|left|4-LOM in the Bakura system]]
Eventually, Zuckuss left the Guild to continue his career alongside 4-LOM,<ref name="Gamer" /> who was eager to continue his study of Zuckuss's meditation.<ref name="NEGTC" /> Around this time, they had scrapped their old ship, which had proved unreliable in the hunt for 12-4C-41, and had acquired a new ship, the [[Mist Hunter/Legends|''Mist Hunter'']], constructed and further modified with undeclared enhancements at the [[Byblos Drive Yards/Legends|Byblos Drive Yards]].<ref name="OSaVC08">[[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 8|''Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection'' 8]]</ref> Financed by a consortium of Gand businessmen, the ''Mist Hunter'' proved effective as a bounty hunting vessel, and 4-LOM and his partner began to rack up numerous bounties in the period that followed. Their good luck brought them back in league with some of the other top bounty hunters, and the two were confident of continued success.<ref name="Gamer" /> Their exploits continued for several years,<ref name="NEGTC" /> and although 4-LOM had yet to master the art of intuition, he continued to observe and question Zuckuss during his meditation rituals.<ref name="Tale" /> 4-LOM himself was highly regarded by many throughout the galaxy, particularly among droids. His fellow hunter, IG-88B, considered recruiting him into his [[Droid Revolution]] for a time, though eventually decided against it, fearing that someone as reckless as 4-LOM was likely to unravel IG-88B's carefully laid plans.<ref name="IG-88">{{StoryCite|story=Therefore I Am: The Tale of IG-88|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref>

{{GameMechanics|legends=1}}
Sometime following the Battle of Yavin, 4-LOM partook in a skirmish against at least one [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]]. 4-LOM was defeated in the fight, but managed to escape alive in his damaged starship.<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesNGE}}</ref>
{{Endgame}}

Around [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]],<ref name="ToppsDate">{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Illustrated: The Empire Strikes Back|cardname=One Year Earlier: 4-LOM|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/112359/cid/7727291/2015-Topps-Star-Wars-Illustrated-The-Empire-Strikes-Back---One-Year-Earlier-OY-15-4-LOM}} dates its events to one [[Standard year/Legends|year]] before those of [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], which ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].</ref> 4-LOM and Zuckuss were hired by the Empire to search the ruins of an ancient temple in the [[Bakura system/Legends|Bakura system]] for relics and weapons that could prove useful in the fight against the Rebellion.<ref name="SWITESB">{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Illustrated: The Empire Strikes Back|cardname=One Year Earlier: 4-LOM|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/112359/cid/7727291/2015-Topps-Star-Wars-Illustrated-The-Empire-Strikes-Back---One-Year-Earlier-OY-15-4-LOM}}</ref>

===Hunt for the ''Millennium Falcon''===
{{Quote|Darth Vader knows what Zuckuss and 4-LOM have done, but he does not care. The acquisitions he sends us to hunt matter more to him&mdash;to the Empire&mdash;than one hundred Governors Nardix: and the Empire needs our help. They know that. Zuckuss and 4-LOM are safe in accepting this contract and the Empire's credits, for now. But if success is not achieved&hellip;|Zuckuss discusses with 4-LOM the duo's assignment for [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]|<ref name="Tale" />}}
The two companions' stretch of success came to an end sometime later when they attempted to capture a routine bounty posted by Jabba. They chased down their quarry, a young Human female, into a dark alley; with nowhere to go, she began to struggle desperately, somehow removing Zuckuss's [[Breath mask/Legends|breathing apparatus]]. 4-LOM secured the acquisition before helping Zuckuss secure his mask, but by then, the Gand had taken in several breaths of [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]], severely damaging his [[Lung/Legends|lungs]]. The cost of an illegal pair of [[Cloning/Legends|cloned]] lungs was considerably expensive, so 4-LOM and his injured friend were once again in dire need of funds.<ref name="Tale" />

The two began taking on as many bounties as they could possibly manage, though Zuckuss's condition meant he was able to contribute little towards each hunt. Gradually, 4-LOM had to perform more and more of the actual work and much of the extra funds they earned had to pay for Zuckuss's painkillers. To Zuckuss's surprise, 4-LOM decided to stay with his partner, despite the fact that he was actually a hindrance to the droid; the two had formed a close friendship and 4-LOM felt that he was becoming increasingly close to learning intuition. They also had to be careful to hide Zuckuss's weakness from potential employers, partners, and rivals, who they knew would take advantage of the Gand's injuries. The pair were so desperate for revenue that they accepted a bounty from the Alliance to Restore the Republic for Imperial [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Nardix]], despite knowing that Imperial retribution would be likely if their involvement was discovered. They captured Nardix, who was put on trial and executed by the Rebels, to the Empire's embarrassment and anger. Though 4-LOM and Zuckuss were paid well for capturing their quarry, they still did not have sufficient money to pay for replacement lungs.<ref name="Tale" />

[[File:4LOMZuckus.jpg|thumb|right|220px|4-LOM and Zuckuss aboard the ''Executor'']]
When [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] and the Empire sent out the call for bounty hunters to assist in the capture of Han Solo&mdash;now an ally of the Rebel Alliance&mdash;Jabba Desilijic Tiure ordered 4-LOM and Zuckuss to liaise with Vader in the [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth system]].<ref name="EGC" /> The two were unsure whether or not the Empire knew of their involvement in the capture of Nardix, though they were unable to resist the possibility of capturing Solo and earning enough money to buy Zuckuss's replacement lungs. Thus, they traveled to [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] in the ''Mist Hunter''. Zuckuss meditated for the entire journey, hoping to discover if Vader knew of their accepting of the bounty on Nardix, while an anxious 4-LOM prepared the ship for an immediate second hyperspace jump in case they were flying into a trap. Eventually, Zuckuss deduced that while Vader did know, he was willing to waive any punishment for the time being, as Solo was more important to him than handing out retribution to the bounty hunters.<ref name="Tale" />

The ''Mist Hunter'' entered [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]] to unexpectedly find itself in the midst of a large [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|battle]]. Eager to appease their Imperial employers, 4-LOM and his partner fired upon the first Rebel ship they encountered, the [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]] [[Bright Hope/Legends|''Bright Hope'']], damaging it severely with one of Zuckuss's intuitive shots. They docked with the [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], Vader's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], and Zuckuss injected himself with an abundance of painkillers so that none aboard would suspect his injuries. On the bridge of the [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]], the duo learned that four other bounty hunters had been assigned to the hunt: their old foes Boba Fett, IG-88B, Bossk, and Dengar. As they departed the [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]], 4-LOM performed intuition for the first time, without having to run any calculations whatsoever: he was able to deduce that Vader was offering them one last chance to redeem themselves over the Nardix affair. Delighted, he made plans to practice intuition, and hoped to use it in the hunt for Han Solo.<ref name="Tale" />

When the two hunters returned to the ''Mist Hunter'', Zuckuss predicted that Solo would travel to the [[Haven (rendezvous point)|Rebel rendezvous point]]; the Gand began meditating with the intention of learning the exact location of the rendezvous, while 4-LOM went to one of the ship's cells to attempt to meditate himself. He produced few results, though at one point the possibility of the Rebels setting up their rendezvous point outside the galaxy entered his mind. His logic programs, however, promptly discounted the possibility. The logic programs were supposed to prevent 4-LOM from thinking an illogical thought; only then did 4-LOM realize that to achieve intuition he had to override logic. He said nothing of his discovery to Zuckuss.<ref name="Tale" />

Several hours after their meeting with Vader, Zuckuss was able to precisely locate the Rebels' location using his findsman abilities. He learned that the Rebels had, remarkably, set their rendezvous point beyond the [[Galactic Rim/Legends|Galactic Rim]]. When Zuckuss discovered that 4-LOM had been attempting to perform intuition, he confronted the droid, accusing him of stealing the Gand's abilities. 4-LOM replied by telling Zuckuss that he did not wish to steal the Gand's intuition, but simply to learn it for himself. The two soon put their squabbling behind them as they set to work formulating a plan. They decided to ambush Solo at the rendezvous point, though knowing they would not be able to simply walk into the base uninvited, 4-LOM and his partner contrived to rescue one of the disabled Rebel transports around Hoth to appease the Rebels. They chose a damaged vessel named the ''Bright Hope''&mdash;the very ship they had helped to disable on their entry to the system.<ref name="Tale" />

===Joining the Rebellion===
{{Quote|There is another way, 4-LOM.''"<br />"''Tell me quickly, then.''"<br />"''Zuckuss has meditated and he has had intuition about what will happen to us. We will not capture Organa or Skywalker. We will end up with a golden, bumbling droid and the two medical droids we brought here, and their bounties will not buy Zuckuss's lungs, nor will turning them over to the Empire clear our names. Both Rebels and Imperials&mdash;and the other bounty hunters&mdash;will hunt us. Zuckuss is sick, and will not survive long without treatment. He has decided to stay here.|Zuckuss persuades 4-LOM to join the Rebel Alliance with him|<ref name="Tale" />}}
4-LOM devised a plan to take several of the Rebels who had the highest bounties and sequester them in the ''Mist Hunter''{{'s}} holding cells for transport to the rendezvous point. They settled on taking twenty-six in total, as their ship could only provide oxygen for that number without affecting Zuckuss. Once there, they would capture Solo and cash in on his and the others' bounties with the Empire. The bounty hunters docked with the ''Bright Hope'' and 4-LOM went aboard to negotiate the "rescue" of several of its occupants. Things became complicated, however, when [[Toryn Farr/Legends|Toryn Farr]], the leading figure among the ship's occupants, proposed an alternate rescue idea: Zuckuss would wear his [[Ammonia/Legends|ammonia]] suit, and the bounty hunters would transfer all of the passengers to their ship for transport to the Rebel underground on Darlyn Boda. 4-LOM was not dissuaded, though, and amid an ensuing scuffle, he dragged Farr onto ''Mist Hunter'', along with several other Rebels. The others resisted and some even began firing on 4-LOM. He took hostages and continued to transfer the beings onto his ship.<ref name="Tale" />

[[File:4-LOM-EGC.jpg|thumb|left|230px|4-LOM, master thief and bounty hunter]]
When 4-LOM returned to the bridge of the ''Mist Hunter'', Zuckuss was furious at him for compromising any chances they had of convincing the Rebels that it was a real rescue attempt. He realized that their only option was to fill the ship with oxygen and allow all the Rebels passage to Darlyn Boda, where the Rebels could be treated in a medical institution. Toryn Farr oversaw the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} evacuation and agreed to travel with the two hunters to the rendezvous point after their trip to Darlyn Boda, where she promised the Rebellion would grow Zuckuss new lungs. 4-LOM reluctantly agreed to the idea, despite the fact that it would further delay their capture of Solo. They eventually arrived on Darlyn Boda&mdash;the very world from where 4-LOM had left his old existence behind and first embarked on a life on crime. Zuckuss's health had rapidly deteriorated, and in an act of kindness rare for the droid, 4-LOM decided to retrieve the Ankarres Sapphire from the old woman he had left it with, hoping its healing properties could help Zuckuss.<ref name="Tale" />

The woman had not sold the precious jewel and 4-LOM retrieved it, giving her one final use of its healing properties before he left. As a way of thanking her for minding it for so long, he allowed the woman to keep the profits she had made selling the droid's other items. The sapphire diminished Zuckuss's injuries and sustained him for the duration of the trip. 4-LOM flew the ''Mist Hunter'' to the rendezvous point while Farr helped Zuckuss cope with his pain. When they reached the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]], Farr told her superiors of 4-LOM's kind actions, while Zuckuss was taken immediately to the [[Medical bay/Legends|medical wing]]. A Rebel [[General/Legends|general]] named [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]] thanked 4-LOM for his actions and offered him and his partner a place in the Rebellion, though 4-LOM decided to wait until Zuckuss was recovered until he made a decision. The bounty hunter droid realized that the respective Rebels he had so far encountered would offer him a goldmine in bounties, though with Zuckuss incapacitated, he had little choice but to wait for the Gand's surgery to be completed. During his stay on the Rebel ship, the [[Redemption/Legends|''Redemption'']], 4-LOM learned that Han Solo had already been captured by Boba Fett and that the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] was on his way to deliver Solo to Jabba the Hutt. Though disappointed, 4-LOM had a back-up plan, which he estimated would make the Empire forgive him and his partner.<ref name="Tale" />

The droid had seen Rebel leaders [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] on the Rebel medical frigate, and proposed to Zuckuss that they kidnap the two Humans and present them to Darth Vader. Zuckuss refused to take any part in it as he was still hospital bound and he did not wish to repay the Rebels' kindness with subterfuge. Although 4-LOM knew his chances of capturing the two alone were slim, he decided to go ahead with his plan and requested that Zuckuss rendezvous with him at their ship at nighttime, at which point 4-LOM would bring Organa and Skywalker.<ref name="Tale" />

[[File:4LOM-NEGTC.png|thumb|right|140px|4-LOM]]
Just before 4-LOM initiated his plan, though, Zuckuss backed out; he had foreseen that they would fail to capture Organa and Skywalker and instead end up with a "[[C-3PO/Legends|golden protocol droid]]" and the two medical droids they had brought to safety. The Rebellion, the Empire, and their fellow bounty hunters would vie for their blood and Zuckuss feared he would not survive. 4-LOM calculated several other options, though one particular scenario stood out to him; that they had a ninety-eight percent chance of establishing the first Bounty Hunter Guild of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. 4-LOM intended to voice this discovery to Zuckuss, though the two were interrupted by Toryn Farr before the droid could reply. Farr had been promoted to the rank of [[Commander/Legends|commander]] and wished to celebrate her appointment with 4-LOM and Zuckuss. The kindness and trust with which they were treated prompted 4-LOM and Zuckuss to join the Rebel Alliance, and they officially became part of the [[Alliance Special Forces/Legends|Alliance Special Forces]]. The ''Mist Hunter'' was refitted as a reconnaissance vessel with advanced technology, and the Rebellion theorized about 4-LOM and Zuckuss possibly rescuing Han Solo, either from Jabba's Palace or before his [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]]-encased body reached there.<ref name="Tale" />

Meanwhile, when he had a free moment, 4-LOM kept practicing his meditation and was slowly proving to be more and more skilled at it. He saw many futures for himself, though one in particular intrigued him; in it, he was sitting with a group of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] in a newly established academy. He was unsure whether he had already learned to use the Force or if he was still attempting to use it in the vision, though he had positive thoughts for the future. He told Zuckuss of his breakthroughs,<ref name="Tale" /> and Luke Skywalker.<ref name="Force">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/81/indexp7.html|text=Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena|int=Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena (article)}}</ref>

===Rebel agent===
{{Quote|4-LOM! There is no point in further resistance!''"<br />"''You're wrong Fett!<!-- Yes, there should be a comma here, but it's not in the original source. The error seems small enough not to merit a [sic] but this note is here to tell you not to "fix" it. --> I can still defeat you!|Boba Fett, with 4-LOM, before the droid was shot in the head|<ref name="SOTE">''[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (comic series)|Shadows of the Empire (comics)]]''</ref>}}
When Zuckuss finally recovered, the duo took a job working alongside several of their peers for [[Domina Tagge/Legends|Domina Tagge]], as a means of establishing their cover as bounty hunters.<ref name="NEGTC" /> Accompanied by Dengar, Bossk and [[IG-88C/Legends|IG-88C]], 4-LOM provided protection for TaggeCo's operatives as they attempted to cause a [[Crimson Forever]] epidemic for both the Alliance and the Empire. On Domina Tagge's ship, they guarded Tagge as she interrogated Leia Organa and Lando Calrissian, though when Calrissian began brandishing his Crimson Fever-infected helmet, the bounty hunters all fled. Tagge's plot was foiled, but it was unimportant to 4-LOM and Zuckuss; the two bounty hunters had managed to conceal their allegiance with the Rebellion.<ref name="Marvel50" /> Afterward, 4-LOM and his partner joined up with a number of prominent bounty hunters who planned to ambush Boba Fett upon his arrival at Tatooine and claim Solo's bounty for themselves. 4-LOM and his partner's mission was to return Solo to the Rebellion, and they managed to keep their ulterior motives secret from Bossk and the others they had teamed up with.<ref name="SOTE" />

[[File:4LOMshot-SOTETC.jpg|thumb|right|180px|4-LOM is shot by Boba Fett.]]
Midway to Tatooine, Fett was ambushed by IG-88C and [[IG-88D/Legends|IG-88D]], and although he managed to destroy the [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droids]]' [[IG-2000/Legends|ships]], the Mandalorian hunter had to stop off at [[Gall/Legends|Gall]] to repair the [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']]. Zuckuss and Bossk made arrangements to meet with Fett on Gall, while 4-LOM and several other bounty hunters forced entry into his ship and began moving Han Solo's carbonite-encased body. Fett, however, realized what Zuckuss and Bossk were planning and rushed back to his ship on a [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bike]]. 4-LOM and his fellows engaged Fett, though the droid was shot in the chest by the Mandalorian. Fett killed the other bounty hunters, and 4-LOM was left in a heap, thought to be disabled.<ref name="SOTE2">[[Shadows of the Empire 2|''Shadows of the Empire'' 2]]</ref> The droid was actually using a tracing signal so that Bossk and Zuckuss could find and intercept the ''Slave I'', which had left Gall and entered [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. Meanwhile, 4-LOM made repairs to himself and left the cargo hold where he had been dumped.<ref name="SOTE3">[[Shadows of the Empire 3|''Shadows of the Empire'' 3]]</ref>

When Zuckuss and Bossk arrived in the [[Hound's Tooth/Legends|''Hound's Tooth'']], Boba Fett realized that 4-LOM was sending them a signal and chased him down one of ''Slave I''{{'s}} corridors, until the droid was cornered. Fett fired on him from point-blank range, severing one of 4-LOM's arms, though the droid was able to destroy the power unit for the ''Slave I''{{'s}} weapon systems. In retaliation, the armored bounty hunter shot 4-LOM in the head, which irreparably damaged his [[Verbobrain/Legends|verbobrain]].<ref name="SOTE3" /> Afterward, Zuckuss, Bossk, Furlag, and two additional hunters&mdash;a [[Unidentified Herglic bounty hunter (Boba Fett)|Herglic]] and a [[Unidentified green-skinned alien bounty hunter|four-armed individual]]&mdash;engaged Fett, though he was able to fend them off and take Zuckuss prisoner.<ref name="SOTE5">[[Shadows of the Empire 5|''Shadows of the Empire'' 5]]</ref> When he reached Tatooine, a host of other bounty hunters were waiting to intercept him and steal Solo for themselves. Fett devised a clever feint, fitting Zuckuss with a suit of his spare armor and chaining him to a speeder bike; 4-LOM was placed under a cover on a [[Hoversled/Legends|hoversled]] and connected to the bike, so that the saboteurs would believe that it was Fett and Solo speeding towards Jabba's Palace. Bossk and the others fell for the ruse and while they gave chase to 4-LOM and Zuckuss, Fett stole into Jabba's Palace unopposed and presented the Hutt with Solo's body.<ref name="SOTE6">[[Shadows of the Empire 6|''Shadows of the Empire'' 6]]</ref>

Fett was paid in full by Jabba, while 4-LOM and his partner were left with nothing.<ref name="SOTE6" /> 4-LOM's verbobrain was left extremely damaged and the only way Zuckuss could fully reactivate his companion was to perform a complete [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipe]]. Only the droid's fourth-degree programming, given to him by Jabba, remained intact, and the idealism that had led him to join the Rebellion was lost. 4-LOM was now a cold, calculating hunter who felt little remorse, and the relationship he and Zuckuss had built up over the years no longer mattered to the droid.<ref name="Gamer" /> Though they did work together for a time,<ref name="Ins99">{{InsiderCite|99|Bounty Hunters' Guild Handbook (article)}}</ref> the droid no longer felt he needed a partner, and set out to pursue his career working solo; he and Zuckuss also severed ties with the Rebellion,<ref name="Gamer" /> though they did not formally leave the organization.<ref name="HM">''[[Hard Merchandise]]''</ref>

===Working solo===
{{Quote|If I didn't need to offset the losses incurred in that botched affair with Boba Fett over Tatooine&hellip;you'd never catch ''me'' risking this&hellip;|4-LOM, while working for Quaffug the Hutt|<ref name="SW">''[[The Bounty Hunters: Scoundrel's Wages]]''</ref>}}
[[File:4-LOMBossk-BHSW.jpg|thumb|left|200px|4-LOM and Bossk chasing Lando Calrissian]]

In order to repay Zuckuss the funds that the Gand had spent in repairing him, 4-LOM took a job working for [[Quaffug]] the Hutt on the [[Tertiary Moon of Blimph|moon]] of [[Blimph]]. Quaffug had managed to capture Lando Calrissian, and desperate to settle an old score with the former [[Gambling/Legends|gambler]], had arranged a competition whereby Calrissian had to escape the bounty hunters before they gunned him down. 4-LOM and his temporary partners, Bossk, [[Guchluk]], and Dengar, gave Calrissian a head start, before beginning to chase him over the volcanic terrain of the moon. Calrissian managed to evade them, though, and reached an area of land controlled by the native [[Jokhalli]]. Although neither 4-LOM nor the other hunters wanted to enter Jokhalli territory, Quaffug offered them double their payment to continue their pursuit of Calrissian and 4-LOM had little choice but to comply. Their efforts failed, however, as Calrissian was able to persuade the Jokhalli to side with him, and took the four mercenaries hostage. He and the natives led an attack on Quaffug's territory, though ultimately the Jokhalli turned on Calrissian and he was forced to flee. 4-LOM and the others were able to escape from their imprisonment and the droid continued to capture bounties for the Hutts.<ref name="SW" />

Shortly after Jabba's death in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], 4-LOM was persuaded by Zuckuss to team up one final time in an attempt to capture a gambler named [[Drawmas Sma'Da]], though the droid only agreed to accept his old partner's assistance because he knew he would be unable to capture the bounty alone. Sma'Da was the creator of a gambling operation that he termed as the "[[Invisible & Ineluctable Casino]]," where patrons could place bets on the ongoing results of the Galactic Civil War. The Empire deduced that he had access to Imperial sources and placed a large bounty on his head; 4-LOM did not immediately tell Zuckuss that it was an Imperial contract, as he was unsure of the Gand's current standing with the Rebels.<ref name="HM" />

Sma'Da frequented an upscale [[Salla C'airam's cantina|cantina]] owned by [[Salla C'airam]], and the two hunters deduced that it was the only location that they would be able to successfully pull off the hunt. C'airam was very strict about bringing weapons into the cantina and had a policy of demanding that patrons hand over the power packs to their blasters upon entrance. 4-LOM and Zuckuss, however, found a way around this: the Gand carried in a powered-down blaster, while 4-LOM used his own modified power source to power the weapon. The two entered the cantina without incident and began the waiting game for Drawmas Sma'Da to arrive.<ref name="HM" />

When Sma'Da entered, 4-LOM had Zuckuss approach him and hold him at blaster point while the powered-down droid stayed in the background. Sma'Da did not take Zuckuss seriously, though, believing that the blaster pointed at him was without a power pack. His opinion on the matter changed drastically when Zuckuss fired a shot just centimeters away from his head. Zuckuss held the gambler hostage, ordering the cantina's staff to find a replacement power pack so that 4-LOM could be reactivated. With his systems fully powered, 4-LOM helped Zuckuss usher Sma'Da out of the establishment; the proprietor, Salla C'airam, told 4-LOM and Zuckuss that they were forever barred from his cantina, though they were allowed to bring Sma'Da to 4-LOM's ship without any opposition. From there, they brought him to the nearest Imperial posting, and cashed in on the gambler's huge bounty.<ref name="HM" />

[[File:4-LOMhtohh.jpg|thumb|right|190px|4-LOM in a cantina]]

===Later existence===
{{Quote|Things aren't what they used to be.''"<br />"''I wouldn't know. Your attitude implies a value judgment on your part. That is, that things were better at one time than they are now. I don't make those kinds of judgments. I merely deal with things as they are.|Zuckuss gets a taste of the new, ruthless 4-LOM|<ref name="HM" />}}
The hunt for Sma'Da proved to be the last time the two worked together, though 4-LOM continued his bounty hunting career working alone.<ref name="Gamer" /> The droid's brief experience of intuition was eventually mentioned in an essay, titled ''[[Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena]]'', written by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Tam Azur-Jamin]] sometime after the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]. 4-LOM's vision of being in the Jedi Academy never came to fruition.<ref name="Force" /> How his late career panned out was not widely documented, though it was known that Drawmas Sma'Da planned to enact his revenge on the duo who had delivered him to [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="HM" />

4-LOM's career as a criminal caused a great deal of embarrassment for his manufacturers. Their rivals, [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]], publicly stated that Industrial Automaton's shoddy workmanship was responsible for 4-LOM's actions, though Industrial Automaton was quick to pin the blame on the ''Kuari Princess''{{'s}} computer. Regardless of who was to blame, 4-LOM's desertion was a public relations fiasco,<ref name="OSaVC" /> and the LOM-series was scrapped not long after 4-LOM's time, making him one of the last active models.<ref name="EGTD" /> A pilot named [[Starter]] bragged about having killed 4-LOM, Zuckuss, Bossk and other bounty hunters, though this was nothing more than an elaborate tall tale.<ref name="Starter's Tale">{{JournalCite|4|Starter's Tale}}</ref>

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|I cannot take your intuition. I hope only to learn to be intuitive myself.|4-LOM reveals his lifelong ambition to Zuckuss|<ref name="Tale" />}}
[[File:4LOM-TTC.jpg|thumb|180px|4-LOM in action|left]]
4-LOM was an ambitious being and spent the majority of his life trying to better equip himself for the job at hand. Through a flaw in his system, he sought to fill his life with challenges and continually altered and overrode his own programming so that he could "help" others. After leaving the ''Kuari Princess'', he set his sights on learning the skill of intuition and partnered himself with Zuckuss. He was very determined to acquire this skill, spending a great many years studying and observing Zuckuss. When he did eventually learn to use intuition, he then decided to master the Force, despite knowing it was illogical.<ref name="Tale" /> When he set out a goal, 4-LOM did his utmost to achieve it, even at his own peril. During the botched attempt to snatch Han Solo from Boba Fett's ship, 4-LOM destroyed Fett's power supply so that Zuckuss might succeed in his assignment, despite knowing that Fett would likely fire on him in retaliation.<ref name="SOTE" />

Both before his entrance into the criminal underworld and after, 4-LOM showed a sort of kindness rare for an emotionless droid. Serving as a steward aboard the ''Kuari Princess'', he took a level of personal pride in helping out the passengers he served. After being altered by the ship's computer, though, he became contemptuous of these beings who had more wealth than sense, and he began to care less and less about their well-being. After becoming a bounty hunter, 4-LOM attempted to hide his kind nature from his peers, so as not to lose out on potential jobs, though he grew very close to Zuckuss. Rather than deserting him, 4-LOM aided the Gand immensely after he became ill, and the droid sacrificed a host of potentially lucrative bounties in order to stay with his partner. 4-LOM also showed much gratitude to the old woman who had safeguarded his stolen gemstones over the years, allowing her to keep his money.<ref name="Tale" />

After his severe damage at the hands of Boba Fett, 4-LOM became a cold, cruel, and heartless being.<ref name="Gamer" /> He no longer cared about his companions, as his only care was for profit. Whereas his past self would only take bounties that he deemed fair, the reactivated 4-LOM took bounties from unscrupulous employers, and cared little about whom he was hunting; he trod on his previous allegiance to the Rebellion, attempting to capture one of its leading officers<ref name="SW" /> and working directly and knowingly for the Empire.<ref name="HM" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|I would prefer it if you did not show any resistance. I have ways of enforcing my preferences.|4-LOM, speaking to one of his targets|<ref name="Fact file">{{FactFile|48|BOU 9-10|Bounty Hunters &ndash; 4-LOM}}</ref>}}
4-LOM preferred to carry arms at all times and usually had several heavy weapons ready to use on unruly quarry or others in his way. His trademark weapon was a long [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|Blastech]] W-90 [[Concussion rifle/Legends|concussion rifle]]<ref name="CCG1">{{CCG|set=Dagobah Limited|cardname=4-LOM's Concussion Rifle}}</ref>&mdash;also called the LJ-90<ref name="Gamer" />&mdash;which he acquired shortly after teaming up with Zuckuss.<ref name="CCG1" /> The rifle was less accurate than the likes of the [[E-11 blaster rifle/Legends|E-11 blaster rifle]], but was far more suited to long-range shooting with a fifty meter range. It required a blaster pack to operate, though the blaster pack had to be replaced after every twenty or so shots.<ref name="Gamer" /> 4-LOM also carried a [[DLT-19 heavy blaster rifle/Legends|DLT-19 heavy blaster rifle]],<ref name="H2H" /> a simple blaster pistol, and a stun gas blower with him for whenever he needed to take an acquisition alive.<ref name="GG3" />

[[File:CCG_Mist_Hunter.jpg|thumb|200px|The ''Mist Hunter'']]
During his career as a bounty hunter, 4-LOM used at least two ships. The first ship had a very fast hyperdrive which proved numerous times to be quicker than the ''Slave I'' and the ''Millennium Falcon'' during the race for the Yavin Vassilika.<ref name="YV" /> Eventually, though, the two hunters decided to purchase another ship; a consortium of wealthy Gand businessmen, impressed with the stories they had heard of Zuckuss's success, had a new ship constructed by Byblos Drive Yards.<ref name="Gamer" /> A fifteen meter [[G-1A starfighter/Legends|G-1A starfighter]], the vessel was a typical bounty hunter ship, though it was far smaller in size than their previous transport. It had a small, two person cockpit, with several acquisition cells and decent-sized living quarters. Zuckuss usually kept the ship pumped full of ammonia so that he would not have to wear his cumbersome breathing suit. After they joined the Alliance Special Forces, 4-LOM and Zuckuss's ship was further modified by the Rebellion, with a [[Sensor mask (starship technology)|sensor mask]], [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]], and concealed weapons added to it. It was unknown who kept the ship after 4-LOM and Zuckuss parted ways, though it was often used to capture bounties for the New Republic.<ref name="Gamer7">{{GamerCite|7|Harbingers of Doom}}</ref>

4-LOM was equipped with a variety of droid features; some were retained from his original function as a protocol droid,<ref name="EGTD" /> while others were the result of his modifications at the hands of Jabba the Hutt, who gave him stronger body armor.<ref name="CCG2">{{CCG|set=Dagobah Limited|cardname=4-LOM}}</ref> His cranial unit contained a variety of sensors and other equipment, including [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]], auditory sensors, a microwave emitter, vocabulator,<ref name="EGTD" /> a broad-band antenna receiver, a [[TranLang III communications module/Legends|TranLang III communications module]], and an [[AA-1 VerboBrain/Legends|AA-1 VerboBrain]].<ref name="GG3" /> The droid was also equipped with [[Servomotor/Legends|servomotors]], [[Recharge coupling/Legends|recharge couplings]], [[powerbus cable]]s, and an [[intermotor actuating coupling]].<ref name="BtM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> 4-LOM was equipped with seven million forms of communication,<ref name="OFC17">{{FigurineCite|17|Droids}}</ref> and was able to speak over four thousand languages, including [[Shyriiwook/Legends|Shyriiwook]], [[Dosh/Legends|Dosh]], [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]], [[Twi'leki/Legends|Ryl]], [[Binary/Legends|binary]], and [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]].<ref name="Gamer" /> He could emit a high-pitched electronic wail, which could serve to disorient any attackers or acquisitions.<ref name="H2H" /> 4-LOM possessed a high intellect and artificial intelligence and was able to provide odds on the outcome of nearly any situation, present or future; this, coupled with Zuckuss's findsman abilities, made for an effective bounty hunting team.<ref name="Tale" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:CloudCityUnknownAlienSpecies.jpg|thumb|200px|A false 4-LOM fights while on Cloud City.|left]]
4-LOM was created for [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], where he was played by [[Chris Parsons]], who also played [[K-3PO/Legends|K-3PO]]. Unlike the other bounty hunters appearing in ''The Empire Strikes Back'', 4-LOM did not appear in the movie's [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novel]]. 4-LOM was made from a variety of different parts of protocol droid costumes originally designed for C-3PO that the set designers of ''The Empire Strikes Back'' cobbled together.<ref name="BtM" /> His name was reportedly an acronym for "for love of money."<ref name="DB" /> There was initially some confusion as to which character was 4-LOM and which was Zuckuss, as their [[Kenner Products|Kenner]] action figures were produced with the names reversed. Eventually, it was decided that 4-LOM should be the droid, and Zuckuss the organic; the [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back|first edition of ''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'']] corrected this error.<ref name="DB" />

In the [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back (junior novelization)|junior novelization]] of ''The Empire Strikes Back'', published in [[October]] of [[2004]], author [[Ryder Windham]] spells 4-LOM's name "4-Lom," with a lowercase "o" and "m." He was described as a "late model protocol droid."<ref name="ESBJN">[[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' junior novelization]]</ref>

Although he debuted in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' in [[1980]], 4-LOM did not receive a proper backstory until [[1989]], with the publication of ''Galaxy Guide 3''.<ref name="GG3" /> This backstory was later fleshed out and expanded upon in ''[[Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM]]'', appearing in ''[[Tales of the Bounty Hunters]]''.<ref name="Tale" /> He has since appeared in several other sources, most of them comics, with a varying personality.<ref name="YV" /><ref name="SOTE" /><ref name="SW" /> ''[[How the Other Half Hunts]]'', an article in [[Star Wars Gamer 6|''Star Wars Gamer'' 6]], explained that his differing personality was because of his memory wipe after the events in [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (comic series)|''Shadows of the Empire'']].<ref name="Gamer" />

In ''[[Super Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', both 4-LOM and Zuckuss are seen fighting alongside IG-88 and Dengar on [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]].<ref name="SSW">''[[Super Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> Later Legends stories established that 4-LOM was on his way to the Rebel rendezvous point during the events of ''The Empire Strikes Back''.<ref name="Tale" />

In the [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|MMORPG]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'', player characters can wear a costume of 4-LOM through the use of a [[Multispectrum disguise suite|holoshroud]].<ref name="Costume Party">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=68775&month=current|text=Friday Feature &ndash; Costume Party Anyone?}}</ref>

In the [[2003]] ''An Empire Divided'' edition of ''Star Wars Galaxies'', 4-LOM was added to the [[Star Wars video games|game]] as a [[Wikipedia:Non-player character|non-player character]] (NPC) in [[W:c:swg:Game Update 20|Game Update 20]]. Players who requested [[W:c:swg:Tier|Tier 7]] [[W:c:swg:Destroy Duty Missions|Duty Missions]] from certain [[Space station/Legends|space stations]] had a chance to battle an [[W:c:swg:Ace Pilot System|elite pilot]] during the mission's boss stage. One of these pilots could be 4-LOM. A player who defeated 4-LOM was not destroyed. Instead, a message indicated that the player successfully defeated the pilot. The player then received a [[W:c:swg:Collection|collection]] icon which added up to award a [[W:c:swg:Badges|badge]] if he or she destroyed all ten elite pilots. Because 4-LOM only appeared in the space portion of ''Star Wars Galaxies'', originally added with the [[Star Wars Galaxies: Jump to Lightspeed|''Jump to Lightspeed'']] expansion pack, he could normally only be seen inside his respective starship. However, a comm display could appear during the battle, displaying 4-LOM's face. In addition, the collection icon depicted 4-LOM's physical appearance. Although players could choose not to participate in any of the battles or collections connected to 4-LOM, this article assumes 100% game completion.<ref name="SWG" />

In a DVD-only segment for ''[[Robot Chicken: Star Wars Episode II]]'', 4-LOM and Zuckuss were depicted answering Emperor Palpatine's bounty-hunter want ad. Zuckuss acted as the duo's fictitious agent while 4-LOM fed lines from nearby. After they secured the contract, 4-LOM and Zuckuss gave each other a high-five and exclaimed, "Dude, we are ''bounty hunters''!" 4-LOM and Zuckuss were voiced by [[Wikipedia:Andy Richter|Andy Richter]] and [[Conan O'Brien]], respectively.<ref name="RCSW2">''[[Robot Chicken: Star Wars Episode II]]''</ref>

In the [[BioWare]] video game ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', an [[Easter egg (virtual)|easter egg]] is included on the bridge of one of starships of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] that recreates the scene on the ''Executor''{{'s}} bridge from ''The Empire Strikes Back''. Darth Vader and the bounty hunters are represented by NPCs that approximate the original characters' appearances; 4-LOM is represented by an assault droid bounty hunter.<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>
